title: get
description: One command for the terminal's common reflexes: what you hand `get` decides what it does — a directory gets listed, a file gets displayed, a word gets grepped, a loose query over a folder becomes a filename search with an fzf pick. The `get` function also owns the cd flow, so cd+ls is one step.

content.heading: get - fast cd+ls workflow for folders, with file viewing and search
content: `get` is a traversal-first helper for the terminal: most invocations are a single `get` away from where you are, and the `-` back-navigation keeps a history of the directories you've been in. The purpose of `get` is to make the cd+ls workflow fast for folders — and it additionally provides support for viewing files in bat, cat, and vim, and supports reading links/PATH items.

`get` is implemented as a bash function (for cd support), backed by `got` — the POSIX-sh script holding all the logic (listing, cat/bat display, grep, filename search + fzf picking, `$PATH` resolution).

`@<name>` is interactive-first: it opens the file in `$EDITOR`. When the session is not a tty (stdin or stdout is piped, as in `cat "$(get @x)"`), `get` skips the editor hijack and prints the canonical resolved path instead — so the caller's own command decides what to do with it.

content.heading: Usage
content: get @name [more...]              open <name> in $EDITOR; if not a local file, resolve it on $PATH and follow symlinks to the real file; non-interactive callers get the resolved path printed instead
get <dir> [names...]             ls the dir, then find each name beneath it
get <queries...> <file|dir>      grep each query (with file+line numbers); for a folder, find matching filenames and fzf-pick one
get <queries...> -- <file|dir>…  same, with an explicit queries/targets split
get -                            cd to the previous directory first
get <dir> [names...]             cd into <dir>, then behave like `got .`

content.heading: Split rule
content: Without `--`: an argument that exists as a file/dir is a target, everything else is a query. If there are no queries at all, targets are displayed; if there are queries, targets are searched.

content.heading: Implementation
content: `get` is implemented as a bash function (for cd support), backed by `got` — the POSIX-sh script holding all the logic (listing, cat/bat display, grep, filename search + fzf picking, `$PATH` resolution).

content.heading: Why two names
content: `got` is a POSIX-sh script, `get` is a thin bash/zsh function wrapping it — a subprocess can't `cd` for you, so the function owns the cd-then-list flow while `got` holds all the viewing/searching logic. The `@<name>` opener degrades gracefully: interactive, it opens `$EDITOR`; piped (scripts, agents, `cat "$(get @x)"`), it prints the canonical resolved path instead.

content.heading: Requirements
content: bat — richer file display; without it, plain cat is used. fzf — the pick UI for folder filename search; without it the search still prints matches.

content.heading: Install
content: Knobs: PREFIX=..., DESTDIR=... (staging), SKIP_RC=1 (files only), RC_FILES="..." (explicit rc list). make uninstall removes the files and strips the rc hooks; make check smoke-tests the tree.
